title: Sprachtest Englisch v2
desc: Lese-/Textverständnis, Vokabeltest, Verben und Orthografie & Grammatik – 20 Aufgaben je Testlauf, 30 Minuten. 50 eigenständige Testläufe (1.000 Aufgaben insgesamt); jeder Testlauf deckt alle 4 Aufgabentypen ab.
intro: Vier Aufgabentypen im Wechsel: (1) Lese-/Textverständnis – zu einem kurzen Text mehrere Aussagen als „correct" oder „not correct" beurteilen; (2) Vokabeltest – eine Lücke im Satz mit dem passenden Wort füllen; (3) Verben – eine Lücke mit der richtigen Form eines von mehreren angegebenen Verben füllen; (4) Orthografie & Grammatik – die korrekt verbesserte Version eines fehlerhaften Satzes auswählen. Jeder Testlauf deckt alle vier Typen ab (6 + 5 + 5 + 4 = 20 Aufgaben).

run1.label: Testlauf 1 – 20 Aufgaben · 30 Min
run1.note: Teil 1 Lese-/Textverständnis (6 Aufgaben zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Vokabeltest (5 Aufgaben), Teil 3 Verben (5 Aufgaben), Teil 4 Orthografie & Grammatik (4 Aufgaben). 30 Minuten für alle 20 Aufgaben.

items.q: The course treats every negotiation as a fixed pie to be divided.
items.e: Nicht richtig – Text sagt das Gegenteil: Optionen sollen „value for both sides“ schaffen, „rather than merely dividing a fixed pie“.
items.passage: Negotiation is a core skill for anyone representing an organisation in dealings with partners, suppliers or authorities. Our two-day workshop trains participants to prepare systematically, to distinguish between positions and underlying interests, and to develop options that create value for both sides rather than merely dividing a fixed pie. Role-plays based on realistic case studies allow participants to practise techniques such as anchoring, active listening and the strategic use of silence. Special attention is given to negotiating across cultures, where directness, the pace of discussion and the role of hierarchy can differ considerably. By the end of the course, participants will be able to plan a negotiation strategy, recognise common tactics used by counterparts, and close agreements that are both fair and sustainable.

items.q: The minister has brushed ____ the accusations, saying he is not in the least worried.
items.e: „to brush aside“ = etwas (eine Anschuldigung, Kritik) beiseiteschieben, nicht ernst nehmen.

items.q: After weeks of talks, the two delegations finally reached an ____ on the border dispute.
items.e: „to reach an agreement“ = eine Einigung erzielen.

items.q: The prime minister flatly ____ any wrongdoing during the press conference.
items.e: „to deny wrongdoing“ = ein Fehlverhalten bestreiten.

items.q: The opposition has ____ the government of covering up the scandal.
items.e: „to accuse somebody of something“ = jemanden einer Sache beschuldigen.

items.q: Following the vote of no confidence, the chancellor was forced to step ____.
items.e: „to step down“ = zurücktreten, sein Amt niederlegen.

items.q: A vicious separatist campaign ____ (launch/plan/debate) by rebels has been raging since 1984.
items.e: Passiv Vergangenheit: „was launched“ (Kampagne wurde gestartet). „Plan“ und „debate“ passen inhaltlich nicht.

items.q: In recent months the group ____ (step/talk/retain) up its attacks considerably.
items.e: Present Perfect: „has stepped up“ = hat verstärkt/intensiviert. Passt zu „in recent months“.

items.q: Few of the provinces ____ (murder/claim/dominate) by the minority are ethnically homogeneous.
items.e: Partizip Perfekt Passiv: „dominated by“ = beherrscht/geprägt von.

items.q: In television debates and across the blogosphere, support for the idea ____ (grow/suggest/accuse) steadily.
items.e: Present Continuous für eine sich entwickelnde Situation: „is growing“.

items.q: The ruling party ____ (plan/deny/retain) to deploy a new professional force along the border.
items.e: Present Simple, 3. Person Singular: „plans to do something“.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „I am living in Bremen since 6 months.“
o: I have lived in Bremen for 6 months.
I live in Bremen since 6 months.
I have lived in Bremen since 6 months.
I am living in Bremen for 6 months.
items.e: Ein bis in die Gegenwart andauernder Zustand mit Zeitdauer verlangt Present Perfect + "for" (nicht "since", das für einen Startzeitpunkt steht).

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „He is working for this company since three years.“
o: He has worked for this company since three years.
He works for this company since three years.
He is working for this company for three years.
He has worked for this company for three years.
items.e: Present Perfect + "for" bei Zeitdauer, nicht Present Continuous + "since".

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „They are living in this house since 2015.“
o: They are living in this house for 2015.
They have lived in this house since 2015.
They have been living in this house from 2015.
They live in this house since the year 2015.
items.e: Present Perfect (Continuous) + "since" bei einem Startzeitpunkt einer andauernden Handlung.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „She is studying medicine since four years.“
o: She is studying medicine for four years.
She has studied medicine since four years.
She has been studying medicine for four years.
She studies medicine since four years.
items.e: Andauernde Handlung mit Zeitdauer: Present Perfect Continuous + "for".

items.q: The ceasefire was declared unilaterally but never took full ____.
items.e: „to take effect“ = wirksam werden, in Kraft treten.

items.q: Negotiators hope to hammer ____ a compromise before the deadline expires.
items.e: „to hammer out a compromise“ = einen Kompromiss mühsam aushandeln.

items.q: The two countries have agreed to a bilateral ____ aimed at reducing tension along the border.
items.e: „ceasefire“ = Waffenstillstand.

items.q: The ambassador was summoned to explain the remarks made by her ____.
items.e: Kontext: die Botschafterin vertritt ihre Regierung ('government') im Ausland.

items.q: The treaty's most controversial provisions were widely ____ by legal scholars.
items.e: „to criticise a provision“ = eine Bestimmung/Klausel kritisieren.

items.q: Thousands of villagers ____ (imprison/suggest/step) during the unrest of the 1990s.
items.e: Passiv Vergangenheit: „were imprisoned“ = wurden inhaftiert.

items.q: Some fighters simply ____ (disappear/debate/claim) without a trace after the crackdown.
items.e: Simple Past: „disappeared“ = verschwanden.

items.q: The allied forces are ____ (provide/murder/plan) intelligence to their partners in the region.
items.e: Present Continuous: „are providing“ = stellen zur Verfügung.

items.q: The party ____ (call/suggest/retain) its programme a bold new opening at the time.
items.e: Simple Past: „called something X“ = etwas X nennen.

items.q: The authorities have been ____ (accuse/plan/talk) local activists of ties to the banned organisation.
items.e: Present Perfect Continuous: „have been accusing“ = beschuldigen seit einiger Zeit.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „We are knowing each other since our school days.“
o: We have known each other since our school days.
We know each other since our school days.
We have been knowing each other since our school days.
We are knowing each other for our school days.
items.e: "know" ist ein Zustandsverb (state verb), daher keine Continuous-Form; Present Perfect + "since" für einen Startpunkt.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „The company is operating in this market since 2010.“
o: The company operates in this market since 2010.
The company has been operate in this market since 2010.
The company is operating in this market for 2010.
The company has operated in this market since 2010.
items.e: Present Perfect + "since" für einen genannten Startzeitpunkt.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „I am waiting for the results since Monday.“
o: I have been waiting for the results since Monday.
I have waited for the results from Monday.
I wait for the results since Monday.
I am waiting for the results for Monday.
items.e: Andauernde Handlung: Present Perfect Continuous + "since" bei Startzeitpunkt.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „He is teaching at this university since 1998.“
o: He teaches at this university since 1998.
He is teaching at this university for 1998.
He has taught at this university since 1998.
He has been teach at this university since 1998.
items.e: Present Perfect + "since" für einen Startzeitpunkt einer andauernden Tätigkeit.

items.q: Hostile questions are said to be avoided entirely during the seminar.
items.e: Nicht richtig – Text sagt das Gegenteil: es wird trainiert, „hostile questions“ ruhig zu beantworten, nicht sie zu vermeiden.
items.passage: Confident public speaking is essential for anyone who must brief superiors, address the media or represent an institution before an audience. This one-day seminar combines short theoretical input with extensive individual practice, all recorded on video for immediate feedback. Participants learn how to structure a presentation around a clear message, how to use voice, pause and gesture deliberately, and how to handle nervousness before and during a talk. A further focus lies on answering difficult or hostile questions calmly, without losing the thread of the argument. Because every participant delivers at least three short presentations during the day, the group size is deliberately kept small, with no more than eight people per course, so that each person receives detailed, individual feedback.

items.q: The president's popularity has slipped amid growing public ____ over the economy.
items.e: „public discontent“ = öffentliche Unzufriedenheit.

items.q: Talks between the two sides broke ____ after just three hours.
items.e: „talks broke down“ = Gespräche scheiterten/wurden abgebrochen.

items.q: The government has come under fire for its handling of the ____.
items.e: „to come under fire for“ = wegen etwas scharf kritisiert werden.

items.q: The reform was passed despite fierce ____ from within the ruling party itself.
items.e: „fierce opposition“ = heftiger Widerstand.

items.q: Diplomats are working around the clock to broker a ____ before the summit ends.
items.e: „to broker a deal“ = einen Deal/eine Einigung vermitteln.

items.q: One senior official has ____ (suggest/deny/murder) that citizens should be treated equally regardless of origin.
items.e: Present Perfect: „has suggested“ = hat vorgeschlagen.

items.q: Despite years in custody, the leader still ____ (retain/disappear/launch) the loyalty of his followers.
items.e: Present Simple, 3. Person Singular: „retains“ = behält.

items.q: Secret ____ (talk/plan/claim) with the imprisoned leader have reportedly been going on for months.
items.e: Nomen im Plural aus dem Verb „to talk“: „talks“ = Gespräche.

items.q: As the prime minister ____ (know/plan/accuse) well, abandoning reform would strengthen his opponents.
items.e: Present Simple, 3. Person Singular: „knows“ = weiß.

items.q: As an old proverb ____ (say/deny/suggest), a stick can have shit at both ends.
items.e: Present Simple, 3. Person Singular: „as the saying goes/as a proverb says“.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „They are negotiating the contract since last week.“
o: They have negotiate the contract since last week.
They have been negotiating the contract since last week.
They negotiate the contract since last week.
They are negotiating the contract for last week.
items.e: Present Perfect Continuous + "since" für den Beginn einer andauernden Handlung.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „We are using this software since two years.“
o: We use this software since two years.
We have used this software since two years.
We are using this software for two years.
We have used this software for two years.
items.e: Present Perfect + "for" bei Zeitdauer.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „I'm just waiting for an taxi.“
o: I'm just waiting for a taxi.
I'm just waiting for an cab.
I'm just waiting for a taxi's.
items.e: "taxi" beginnt mit einem Konsonantenlaut, daher "a taxi", nicht "an taxi".

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „She works as an nurse in the local hospital.“
o: She work as a nurse in the local hospital.
She works as a nurse's in the local hospital.
She works as a nurse in the local hospital.
She works as an nurses in the local hospital.
items.e: "nurse" beginnt mit einem Konsonantenlaut: "a nurse".

items.passage: Confident public speaking is essential for anyone who must brief superiors, address the media or represent an institution before an audience. This one-day seminar combines short theoretical input with extensive individual practice, all recorded on video for immediate feedback. Participants learn how to structure a presentation around a clear message, how to use voice, pause and gesture deliberately, and how to handle nervousness before and during a talk. A further focus lies on answering difficult or hostile questions calmly, without losing the thread of the argument. Because every participant delivers at least three short presentations during the day, the group size is deliberately kept small, with no more than eight people per course, so that each person receives detailed, individual feedback.

items.passage: Most successful cyber-attacks on organisations begin not with a technical flaw but with a single careless click. This half-day course raises awareness among staff of all levels about phishing e-mails, fraudulent phone calls and the manipulation techniques known as social engineering. Using real, anonymised examples, participants learn to recognise suspicious messages, to verify unusual requests through a second channel, and to report incidents immediately rather than trying to fix them alone. The course also covers safe practices for mobile devices, public Wi-Fi networks and password management, including the use of a password manager. Given how quickly attack methods evolve, we recommend refreshing this training every twelve months, and offer a short online update course for returning participants.

items.q: Accessible workplace design is mentioned as a way to remove barriers.
items.e: Richtig – Text: „accessible workplace design can remove barriers“.
items.passage: Organisations that draw on the full range of their employees' backgrounds and perspectives make better decisions and are more resilient to change. Our diversity and inclusion programme begins by helping participants recognise unconscious bias in recruitment, promotion and everyday interactions. Interactive exercises then explore how inclusive language, flexible meeting formats and accessible workplace design can remove barriers for colleagues with disabilities, different cultural backgrounds or caring responsibilities. The programme deliberately avoids a one-off lecture format; instead, it is delivered as three shorter sessions spread over several weeks, allowing participants to try out new behaviours between sessions and to discuss what worked and what did not. Managers attend an additional session on inclusive leadership and fair performance evaluation.

items.q: The trainers claim time management is mainly a collection of tricks.

items.passage: Many professionals feel busy all day yet finish it without making progress on what matters most. This one-day workshop addresses that gap between activity and achievement. Participants learn to distinguish urgent tasks from important ones, to plan their week around a small number of priorities rather than an ever-growing list, and to protect blocks of undisturbed time for demanding work. Practical sessions cover techniques for handling e-mail more efficiently, for saying no to low-value requests without damaging relationships, and for delegating tasks appropriately. The trainers emphasise that time management is ultimately a matter of decisions about priorities, not a collection of tricks, and that no technique will help someone who has not first clarified their actual goals.

items.q: Case studies are drawn from real cross-border projects.

items.passage: Working across borders means working across assumptions that are rarely made explicit. This training helps staff who cooperate with international partners understand how communication styles, attitudes to time, and ways of giving feedback vary between cultures, and, more importantly, how to adapt without abandoning one's own professional standards. Through case studies drawn from real cross-border projects, participants examine misunderstandings that arose from differing expectations about punctuality, hierarchy and directness of speech. The course does not offer a checklist of national traits, which the trainers regard as an oversimplification; instead, it teaches a general approach of curiosity, observation and asking clarifying questions before drawing conclusions about a colleague's behaviour.

items.passage: A single poorly handled interview can undo months of careful communication work. This media training prepares spokespeople and executives for interviews with journalists, whether in front of a camera, on the radio, or in writing. Participants first learn to define three key messages before any interview and to return to them regardless of the question asked, a technique known as bridging. Simulated interviews, conducted by a former journalist and recorded on camera, allow participants to experience the pressure of a real interview and to receive frank feedback on body language, tone and clarity. The course also addresses how to handle hostile or repeated questions calmly and how to correct a factual error made live without appearing evasive.

items.passage: Organisational change fails far more often because of resistance among staff than because of a flawed plan. This training equips managers to lead their teams through periods of restructuring, new systems or merged departments. Participants examine typical phases of reaction to change, from initial denial through resistance to eventual acceptance, and learn techniques to communicate a compelling reason for change early and repeatedly. The training also covers how to identify informal opinion leaders within a team and to win their support before a wider rollout.

items.q: Identifying, assessing, responding to and monitoring risks are the four steps.

items.passage: No plan survives contact with reality unchanged, which is why systematic risk management matters as much for a small project as for an entire organisation. This one-day seminar introduces a simple four-step process: identifying risks, assessing their likelihood and potential impact, deciding on a response, and monitoring the risk throughout the project. Participants practise the process using realistic scenarios drawn from logistics, IT and public administration. A recurring theme of the seminar is that risks should be owned by a named person, not left as a vague shared responsibility, and that a risk register is only useful if it is reviewed regularly rather than filed away after being created.

items.passage: Executive coaching offers senior staff a confidential space to reflect on challenges that are difficult to discuss openly within their own organisation. Unlike training, which teaches skills to a group, coaching is a one-to-one process tailored to the individual's specific situation, typically delivered over six to eight sessions across several months. A coach does not give direct advice on what decision to make; instead, the coach asks questions that help the client clarify their own thinking, examine blind spots and consider options they may not have considered. Confidentiality is central to the process: coaches do not report the content of sessions to the client's employer, only, where agreed in advance, a brief summary of overall progress.

A coach does not give direct advice on what decision to make; instead, the coach asks questions that help the client clarify their own thinking, examine blind spots and consider options they may not have considered. Confidentiality is central to the process: coaches do not report the content of sessions to the client's employer, only, where agreed in advance, a brief summary of overall progress.

items.q: Toasts and formal introductions are not mentioned in the course.
items.e: Nicht richtig – Text sagt das Gegenteil: „the handling of toasts and formal introductions“ wird genannt.
items.passage: Diplomatic and official events follow conventions that, while sometimes appearing formal or old-fashioned, exist to avoid misunderstandings and to show appropriate respect. This course prepares staff who represent their institution at receptions, state visits or official dinners for the practical questions of protocol: correct forms of address, seating order according to rank, and appropriate dress for different occasions. Particular attention is paid to how gifts are exchanged and accepted in different diplomatic traditions, and to the handling of toasts and formal introductions. The course stresses that protocol should never be applied rigidly for its own sake; its underlying purpose is always to put guests at ease and to prevent avoidable offence.

items.q: The company's new policy has been widely ____ by employees as a step forward.
items.e: „to welcome a policy“ = eine Maßnahme begrüßen.

items.q: The department was ____ with implementing the new compliance framework.
items.e: „to be tasked with doing something“ = mit etwas beauftragt werden.

items.q: The firm's quarterly results ____ analysts' expectations by a wide margin.
items.e: „to exceed expectations“ = die Erwartungen übertreffen.

items.q: The new hires will ____ a six-month probationary period before permanent contracts are issued.
items.e: „to undergo a probationary period“ = eine Probezeit durchlaufen.

items.q: The company was praised for its ____ approach to sustainability.
items.e: „proactive approach“ = vorausschauendes/proaktives Vorgehen.

items.q: The minister ____ (insist/deny/suggest) that the report had been taken out of context.
items.e: Simple Past: „insisted that“ = bestand darauf, dass.

items.q: The whistleblower was commended for ____ (reveal/deny/suggest) the fraud after years of silence.
items.e: Gerundium nach „commended for“: „for revealing“.

items.q: An initial holding statement ____ (acknowledge/deny/suggest) the situation without speculating on causes.
items.e: Present Simple, 3. Person Singular: „acknowledges“ = erkennt an, räumt ein.

items.q: The team is ____ (monitor/deny/suggest) social media for rumours that may need addressing.
items.e: Present Continuous: „is monitoring“ = beobachtet gerade.

items.q: A full-day simulation has ____ (put/deny/suggest) participants through a realistic crisis scenario.
items.e: Present Perfect: „has put somebody through something“ = hat jemanden durch etwas gehen lassen.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „They did a lot of progress on the project this month.“
o: They did a lot of progresses on the project this month.
They do a lot of progress on the project this month.
They making a lot of progress on the project this month.
They made a lot of progress on the project this month.
items.e: "make progress" ist die feste Kollokation, nicht "do progress".

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „Please do an effort to arrive on time next week.“
o: Please making an effort to arrive on time next week.
Please make effort to arrive on time next week.
Please do an efforts to arrive on time next week.
Please make an effort to arrive on time next week.
items.e: "make an effort" ist die feste Kollokation, nicht "do an effort".

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „The team did a great job doing the presentation.“
o: The team did a great job on the presentation.
The team does a great job doing the presentation.
The team made a great job doing the presentation.
The team did great job doing the presentation.
items.e: "do a great job on something" ist die richtige Präposition; "doing the presentation" ist hier überflüssig/falsch strukturiert.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „We should do some research before doing a final decision.“
o: We should make some research before doing a final decision.
We should do some research before to do a final decision.
We should do some research before making a final decision.
We should do some researches before doing a final decision.
items.e: "do research" aber "make a decision" – beide Kollokationen dürfen nicht vertauscht werden.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „He makes business with several companies abroad.“

He make business with several companies abroad.
He makes businesses with several companies abroad.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „She did a good job of making the arrangements for the trip.“

She did good job of making the arrangements for the trip.
She made a good job of doing the arrangements for the trip.
She did a good job of making the arrangements for the trip.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „We don't have much problems with the new system.“

We haven't much problems with the new system.
We don't have many problems with the new system.

items.e: "problems" ist zählbar (Plural): "many problems", nicht "much problems".

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „There were less applicants this year than last year.“

There were least applicants this year than last year.
There were fewer applicants this year than last year.
There was less applicants this year than last year.
items.e: "applicants" ist zählbar: "fewer", nicht "less".

items.q: The seminar claims digital transformation is simply about introducing new software.
items.e: Nicht richtig – Text sagt das Gegenteil: „often misunderstood as simply introducing new software“.
items.passage: Digital transformation is often misunderstood as simply introducing new software, when in fact the greater challenge lies in changing working habits and decision-making processes. This seminar helps non-technical managers understand the opportunities and limits of automation, data analysis and digital collaboration tools, without requiring any programming knowledge. Case studies show how organisations have used digital tools to speed up routine approvals, to make decisions based on real data rather than assumption, and, in some cases, to fail expensively by digitising a broken process instead of first fixing it. Participants leave with a simple framework for judging whether a proposed digital initiative addresses a genuine problem or merely follows a passing trend.

items.q: The manager was ____ (coach/deny/suggest) through the process by an experienced mentor.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „How much people attended the conference this year?“

How many peoples attended the conference this year?

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „The company has much competitors in this sector.“

The company has many competitors in this sector.

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „We received less complaints after the update.“

items.q: Identify the correct version of: „There are much options available for this route.“

There are many option available for this route.

A full-day simulation puts participants through a realistic, fast-moving crisis scenario.

items.passage: Cross-border trade involves a web of rules that can trap the unwary, from customs classification to export controls on sensitive goods. This course gives non-lawyers a working understanding of the key legal concepts involved in international trade, including the difference between tariffs and non-tariff barriers, the basic structure of trade agreements, and the compliance obligations that arise when exporting controlled technology. Case studies illustrate the consequences of misclassifying goods or overlooking a licensing requirement, including significant fines and reputational damage. The course does not train participants to replace legal counsel, but to recognise situations that require it, and to ask legal or compliance colleagues the right questions early, before a shipment is already in transit.

items.q: Consular staff are described as the first point of contact for citizens in difficulty abroad.

items.passage: Consular staff are often the first point of contact for citizens facing the most difficult moments of their lives abroad, from lost documents to serious accidents or arrest. This training prepares new consular officers for the practical and emotional demands of the role. Participants practise handling distressed callers with empathy while gathering the precise information needed to act, and learn the procedures for emergency passports, next-of-kin notification, and liaison with local authorities and hospitals. The course stresses the limits of consular assistance: officers can offer support and advocate for fair treatment, but cannot interfere in another state's legal proceedings or guarantee a particular outcome. Self-care for staff who regularly handle distressing cases is also addressed.

items.passage: A certain amount of pressure can sharpen performance, but sustained stress without recovery eventually undermines health, judgement and working relationships. This training helps staff in demanding roles recognise the early warning signs of chronic stress in themselves and in colleagues, before these develop into burnout. Participants learn practical techniques for regulating their response under pressure, including structured breathing exercises and brief attention resets between demanding tasks, as well as longer-term habits such as protecting recovery time and setting realistic boundaries around availability outside working hours. The course explicitly does not treat resilience as simply enduring more pressure silently; instead, it frames resilience as the ability to recover well and to seek support early, before a crisis develops.

run50.label: Testlauf 50 – 20 Aufgaben · 30 Min
run50.note: Teil 1 Lese-/Textverständnis (6 Aufgaben zu einem Textabschnitt), Teil 2 Vokabeltest (5 Aufgaben), Teil 3 Verben (5 Aufgaben), Teil 4 Orthografie & Grammatik (4 Aufgaben). 30 Minuten für alle 20 Aufgaben.

items.q: Brief attention resets between tasks are part of the techniques taught.
items.e: Richtig – Text: „brief attention resets between demanding tasks“.
items.passage: A certain amount of pressure can sharpen performance, but sustained stress without recovery eventually undermines health, judgement and working relationships. This training helps staff in demanding roles recognise the early warning signs of chronic stress in themselves and in colleagues, before these develop into burnout. Participants learn practical techniques for regulating their response under pressure, including structured breathing exercises and brief attention resets between demanding tasks, as well as longer-term habits such as protecting recovery time and setting realistic boundaries around availability outside working hours. The course explicitly does not treat resilience as simply enduring more pressure silently; instead, it frames resilience as the ability to recover well and to seek support early, before a crisis develops.

items.q: The commission has the authority to ____ a member's voting rights in serious breaches.
items.e: „to suspend voting rights“ = Stimmrechte aussetzen.

items.q: The company was ____ to pay a substantial fine for the breach.
items.e: „to be ordered to do something“ = dazu verurteilt/angewiesen werden, etwas zu tun.

items.q: The tribunal's ruling is expected to ____ far-reaching consequences for the sector.
items.e: „to have consequences“ = Konsequenzen haben.

items.q: The inquiry was eventually ____ after both sides reached a private settlement.
items.e: „to close an inquiry“ = eine Untersuchung einstellen.

items.q: The government's proposal has been dismissed as too little, too ____.
items.e: „too little, too late“ = zu wenig und zu spät.

items.q: The minister's statement was ____ (see/deny/suggest) as a thinly veiled dig at his rival.
items.e: Passiv Vergangenheit: „was seen as“.

items.q: The two leaders ____ (agree/deny/suggest) to hold talks on the sidelines of the summit.
items.e: Simple Past: „agreed to do something“.

items.q: The delegation's visit was widely ____ (see/deny/suggest) as a sign of thawing relations.
items.e: Passiv Vergangenheit: „was seen as a sign of“.

items.q: The government has ____ (reiterate/deny/suggest) its support for the peace initiative.
items.e: Present Perfect: „has reiterated support“ = hat Unterstützung erneut bekräftigt.

items.q: The two blocs have agreed to ____ (ease/deny/suggest) restrictions as part of the new pact.
items.e: Infinitiv nach „agreed to“: „to ease restrictions“.
